entries.title: II Kings 17:2
segments:
Not as the kings of Israel; he did not so rigidly enforce idolatry. 
 
Some sinners are less atrociously wicked than others; yet none are so innocent as not to deserve all the evils they suffer in this world, and still more dreadful evils in the world to come.

entries.title: II Kings 17:6
segments:
Halah; probably one of the northern provinces of Assyria. 
 
  In Habor by the river of Gozan; or, by Habor, the river of Gozan. Habor is generally thought to be the ancient Chaboras, a river of Mesopotamia, which flows into the Euphrates, (the modern Khabur,) and Gozan, a province situated on this river.  Some, however, place Habor and Gozan farther east. 
 
Though God bears long with guilty nations, if they repent not of their iniquities he will eventually destroy them.

entries.title: II Kings 17:9
segments:
From the tower of the watchmen to the fenced city; that is, from the least to the greatest of their dwelling-places, the tower of the watchmen being a solitary building, where only the watchman and his dependents lived. 
 
Wicked as are the outward actions of men, their secret conduct is often much worse, and has greater influence in drawing down upon them the just judgments of heaven.

entries.title: II Kings 17:10
segments: Groves; here, as often elsewhere, the original word means an image of Astarte.  See

entries.title: II Kings 17:13
segments: Men do not go to destruction without warning from God, and their disregard of him and his threatenings is among the chief causes of their ruin.

entries.title: II Kings 17:15
segments: Vanity; here used, as frequently elsewhere, to describe idolatry.

entries.title: II Kings 17:17
segments: No wickedness is so great that it may not be committed by those who have light, but reject it; who know the will of God, and yet refuse to do it.

entries.title: II Kings 17:18
segments: The tribe of Judah only; comprehending at this time the tribe of Benjamin.

entries.title: II Kings 17:24
segments: Cuthah--Ava--Hamath--Sepharvaim; provinces of Assyria north-east of Palestine.

entries.title: II Kings 17:25
segments: Even the heathen, though not as guilty as sinners under the gospel, know, or have the means of knowing, enough of God to render them guilty in not obeying him.

entries.title: II Kings 17:26
segments: The manner of the God; the proper way of worshipping him.

entries.title: II Kings 17:29
segments: Though unconverted heathen may be brought to pay a kind of reluctant outward homage to Jehovah yet without his grace their hearts will cleave to their idols, and they will still make and worship the gods to which they have been accustomed.

entries.title: II Kings 17:30
segments:
vv 30-31. 
 
  Succoth-benoth--Nergal--Ashima--Nibhaz and Tartak; names of different heathen gods.

entries.title: II Kings 17:33
segments: Feared the Lord, and served their own gods; they feared Jehovah, not as the only true God, with filial reverence and obedience to all his commands, but only as one god--the god of that particular land--among many other gods.  Supposing that he had special power in his own land, they feared his wrath and sought to appease him with outward services, while they still clung each to the worship of his own god.

entries.title: II Kings 17:34
segments:
They fear not the Lord; not with a true fear and love, as the only true God. 
 
  After their statutes; after their own idolatrous statutes.  Their religion is neither the pure worship of Jehovah, nor pure idolatry, but a mixture of the two.  This people are supposed to have been the ancestors of the Samaritans mentioned in the New Testament.

entries.title: II Kings 17:40
segments: No instruction in the knowledge and worship of God will of itself lead men to love and obey him, or prevent them from practising those sins which provoke him to destroy them.
